name: CloudBurst San Marcos Data Center I

profile.address: 2955 Francis Harris Lane, San Marcos, TX 78666 (Hays and Guadalupe counties)
profile.reading:
San Marcos Data Center I is CloudBurst Data Centers' flagship campus in the San Marcos and New Braunfels corridor of Central Texas, straddling Hays and Guadalupe counties between Austin and San Antonio. CloudBurst and its builder Evolve Holdings broke ground on 5 November 2025. The campus is master planned for up to 1.2 GW of AI and high-performance compute, with a first 50 MW phase due in the fourth quarter of 2026.

Power is behind the meter from natural gas. CloudBurst has a ten-year agreement with Energy Transfer for up to 450,000 MMBtu a day of firm gas via the Oasis Pipeline, which the companies say could generate more than 1.8 GW on site. Local reporting notes this reversed an earlier renewable energy pledge.

The 1.2 GW is the developer's master plan, not built capacity. Coordinates are a Nominatim geocode of the street address.

reading.body:
CloudBurst's San Marcos campus is a 1.2 GW gas-fired AI data center master plan with only 50 MW actually scheduled, a gap that shows how far announced capacity runs ahead of construction.

The campus broke ground on 5 November 2025 and its first 50 MW phase is targeted for the fourth quarter of 2026. The 1.2 GW figure is the developer's master plan, not built capacity. That distinction matters because the site's power is behind the meter from natural gas, under a ten-year Energy Transfer agreement for up to 450,000 MMBtu a day via the Oasis Pipeline, which the companies say could generate more than 1.8 GW on site. Local reporting notes the gas arrangement reversed an earlier renewable energy pledge.

For AI specifically, this is a template for how compute scaling is now sited: not where the grid is strongest, but where a firm fuel supply and a pipeline can be contracted directly. The generation figure exceeds the campus plan, so the binding constraint here is not fuel or land but the pace of building the first phase. The data does not say whether the 1.2 GW will ever be built, what the gas contract costs, or how the campus connects to the ERCOT grid, if at all. It covers one facility in the San Marcos and New Braunfels corridor, not the region's aggregate load.
